# Capital of France facts for kids
The **capital of France** is Paris.
A country's capital city is usually where its government is located.
While Paris is the capital today, France has had many different capital cities throughout its long history.
...
## History of France's Capitals
### Where France's Capital Has Been
- Paris (1594—1661)
- Paris (1661-1682) Paris was the official capital.
But King Louis XIV wanted Versailles to be the main political center.
- Versailles (1682–1715) In 1682, King Louis XIV moved his royal home to Versailles.
- Paris (1715–1722)
- Versailles (1722–1789) In 1789, people from Paris marched to Versailles.
They forced the royal family to move back to Paris.
The National Assembly, which was the government, also moved to Paris.
This made Versailles lose its role as the capital.
- Paris (1789–1871)
- Versailles (1871–1879) After the Paris Commune took control of Paris, the new French government (the French Third Republic) moved its base to Versailles in March 1871.
- Paris (1879–1914, 1914-1940)
- Bordeaux (September 1914) At the start of World War I, the French government briefly moved from Paris to Bordeaux.
They were worried Paris might be captured by German forces.
These fears ended after the Germans were pushed back at the First Battle of the Marne.
- Tours (10–13 June 1940) During World War II, Tours was a temporary capital.
The government fled Paris because of the German army's advance.
- Bordeaux (June 1940) The French government moved again from Tours to Bordeaux.
This happened very quickly as it became clear Paris would soon fall to Germany.
- Vichy (1940-1944) The French Parliament met here and changed the government to the French State.
- Paris (1944–present) When Paris was freed in 1944, Charles de Gaulle set up a new government.
This brought Paris back as the capital of France.

Before Paris, the capital of France

# Paris History: Complete Historical Guide
## Key Takeaways
- Paris evolved from the Celtic Parisii settlement on Île de la Cité in 250 BCE through Roman Lutetia, medieval capital, Renaissance glory, and revolutionary transformation into modern metropolis
- The city’s strategic Seine River location enabled 2,000+ years of continuous occupation, trade dominance, and political power as capital of France since 987 CE

## People Also Ask About Paris History
### Why did Paris become the capital of France?
Paris established itself as France’s permanent capital through the convergence of geography, royal preference, and political necessity.
Clovis I, first king of the Franks to convert to Christianity, selected Paris as his capital in 508 CE, recognizing the city’s central location, defensible island core, and river transportation advantages.
The Capetian dynasty, beginning with Hugh Capet in 987 CE, solidified Paris as the undisputed capital and royal residence, with successive monarchs making the city the center of political authority, justice, and administration.
...
## Medieval Paris and Capetian Capital
### Merovingian and Carolingian Periods
Clovis I’s selection of Paris as Frankish capital in 508 CE initiated the city’s medieval transformation from provincial Roman town to political center of emerging French kingdom.
...
### Capetian Dynasty and Gothic Flowering
Hugh Capet’s election as King of France in 987 CE established Paris as the permanent capital of a dynasty lasting until 1328 (direct male line) and 1848 (through Capetian branches).
...
## FAQ Section
### When did Paris become France’s capital?
Paris became France’s capital gradually rather than through single decisive moment.
Clovis I selected Paris as his Frankish capital in 508 CE, giving the city early political importance.
Hugh Capet’s election as King of France in 987 CE established Paris as the fixed seat of royal power and permanent capital, a status maintained through subsequent dynasties and regime changes.
The Capetian choice reflected Paris’s central location, defensible position, economic importance, and growing prestige as intellectual and religious center.

# Paris in the Middle Ages: This is how the capital of the Kingdom of France was born
- **The moment Paris became the capital:** During the Carolingian period, the capital moved to Aachen and Paris lost its status.
The coronation of Eugène Capa brought it back to the center, and within about a hundred years it became the de facto capital.
- **The Viking Siege:** In 885–886, Count Odo (Eudes) successfully defended the city, and as a result was crowned King of France.
- **What kings built:** Philippe Auguste erected the first wall of Paris (remains in the Marais district and behind the Pantheon), Louis IX built Sainte-Chapelle, and Charles V built the Bastille, the Château de Vincennes, and a new wall.
...
## Early Middle Ages: 486-987
During the Carolingian period, Paris declined in status, and the capital was moved to Aachen (Aix La Chapelle).

## Late Middle Ages: 987-1483
In 987, when Ige Cappa came to power, Paris was a relatively small city.
Viking raids had caused the left bank to be abandoned, and the population had concentrated on the fortified island, the Île de la Cité.
However, as Paris was now the king's capital, its position grew, and within about a century it had become the capital of the kingdom not only in name but also in practice.
